A modern Guiche 22 November 1551 study claims key recovery and a substantial partial reading. These claims prevent new-target admission; exact folio/source-region matches remain unverified.
case_holds.remaining: Retain separate item IDs and prior exclusions; do not count known-answer reproduction as a new decipherment.

case_holds.remaining: Usable transcription, original-source correspondence, exact prior clearance and method qualification. Authentication requirements were not established.

case_holds.remaining: Exclude both from the new-attack queue. This is an attributed prior claim, not an independently verified decryption or a new local result.

case_holds.remaining: Exact modern claim-to-letter identity and source qualification remain incomplete.

case_holds.remaining: Complete source, exact artifact identity, current prior clearance, language and matched method are unqualified. No transcription ledger or target trial.

case_holds.remaining: Individual letter identities, original readable sources and exact modern prior-reading checks remain unqualified. Collection-level descriptions do not establish eight new open targets.

identity_guard_correction.effect: Exact parent aliases and related child IDs must also be screened. A shared alias is a review hold, never permission for a new attack or automatic same-message merging.

limits: One-page catalogue checks do not certify global completeness or enforcement of server filters.
Administrative exclusions are not counts of attempted or solved ciphers.
Missing source access is not evidence that a cipher is mathematically unsolvable.

timing_exceptions.interpretation: These completed observations are retained with their scope and deadline exceptions; no timing compliance PASS or cryptanalytic failure is asserted.
